subject.title: [Bug]: MidTurnPrecheckSignal leaks error to UI via pushLoopFailure before internal retry completes

question: Should the durable fix introduce a documented generic agent-core control-flow error contract, or keep `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` handling inside the embedded-runner boundary?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the current fix candidate changes reusable agent-core failure semantics; maintainers need to choose that boundary before this issue can close safely.

options.title: Formalize the core seam first
options.body: Expose or document a generic agent-core control-flow contract, align the transform hook contract, and require tests proving marked control-flow errors are suppressed while real failures still emit terminal events.

options.title: Keep it runner-owned
options.body: Handle or prevent the signal inside the embedded runner so agent-core continues treating thrown transform errors as ordinary failures.

options.title: Accept the current sentinel after proof
options.body: Allow the current hidden-symbol approach after live proof, with maintainers explicitly owning the new Agent failure-event semantics.

recommendation.title: Formalize the core seam first
recommendation.body: Expose or document a generic agent-core control-flow contract, align the transform hook contract, and require tests proving marked control-flow errors are suppressed while real failures still emit terminal events.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the mid-turn precheck path and have the strongest feature-history signal for the runner boundary.
